title: Hoover Dam's Concrete Would Have Needed 125 Years to Cool

scenes.text: Hoover Dam's concrete would have needed 125 years to cool.
Engineers found that one giant pour would stay hot for over a century.
The heat and shrinking could have cracked the dam.
So they poured it in blocks and let each one cool first.
They ran river water through 582 miles of steel pipes inside the concrete.
The dam cooled itself with hidden pipes. Watch it again.

description:
A single continuous pour of Hoover Dam's concrete would have taken about 125 years to cool.
So engineers built it in blocks and ran river water through more than 582 miles of cooling pipes.
Would you have thought of the pipes?
first_comment: What's the most impressive structure you've ever seen in person?
